stories.title: She spent nearly 20 years believing she had MS. Then her diagnosis changed.
stories.summary: DeMonica Amerson was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis at 21. Nearly two decades later, she received devastating news. DeMonica Amerson's diagnosis of multiple sclerosis in 2001 had been a shock. No one in her family had ever had the autoimmune condition, and it had been difficult to diagnose. Doctors had first thought she had optic neuritis because her symptoms were in her eyes. Then they suspected lupus. After a spinal tap, she was diagnosed with MS. At the time, Amerson had never heard about the condition. She had just graduated from college and expected to be in the prime of her life. Instead, she had to give herself daily shots to treat the condition.

stories.title: Dodgers Arbitration Decisions: 4 Locks and 2 Players on the Bubble
stories.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers have six players entering arbitration this offseason, and they need to decide how to approach them. The standard number of arbitration years is three, but players in the top 22% can earn the Super Two Exception, which lets them enter arbitration a year early and get four total years. In arbitration, a team must decide whether to tender or non-tender players by November 20th. If they are tendered, they continue to arbitration; if they are non-tendered, they become free agents. Once tendered, the team and player can agree to avoid arbitration or go to a hearing, where both sides submit a salary proposal and a third-party arbitrator rules for the player or team.
